output.summary: KEP-1731 proposes publishing deb and rpm Kubernetes packages on community infrastructure, generated and published automatically by the release tooling (krel) as part of cutting each release, with stable, dev and nightly channels. Its status is implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale: Publishing packages depended on a small group of Googlers and Google infrastructure, and was paused the release announcement. The KEP folds package builds and publishing into release tooling so only release managers are involved. The source describes the proposal but gives no account of the reasoning behind the chosen alternative infrastructure.

alternatives.option: Keep publishing packages on Google infrastructure by Googlers
alternatives.why_not: The source lists this as the current problem: "Only Googlers can publish packages." and "The packages get published on Google infrastructure."

alternatives.option: Use a Packages as a Service solution (e.g. Open Build Service) instead of building infrastructure manually
alternatives.why_not: Listed as an option in the proposal, not rejected; the source does not say which option was chosen.

alternatives.option: Generate packages under a separate KEP (pkg-gen-kep, PR 858)
alternatives.why_not: Non-Goals say the package generation is a different problem, and that sig-release ownership of the build and publish process was requested by @saschagrunert, implicitly achieving #2503.

evidence.quote: Only Googlers can publish packages. - The packages get published on Google infrastructure.
The whole process should be folded into the release tooling, it should be part of the release process, and should not involve anyone other than the release managers.
There should be multiple channels users can subscribe to: **stable**, **dev**, and **nightly**.
Based on a review of this KEP, Kubernetes contributor @saschagrunert wants SIG Release to own the process of automatically building and publishing the packages
